summary: A concrete tower on a Palos Verdes cliff, authorised in 1915 but held up for a decade by a land dispute; the fog signal began in 1925 and the light in 1926.

lens.where: Point Vicente Interpretive Center (loaned by the Coast Guard since 2019)

access.note: Coast Guard property; grounds and fog signal building museum open on the second Saturday of each month 10 a.m.-3 p.m. (Coast Guard Auxiliary open house); dwellings closed.

notes_for_editor: Tower height disagrees: Bulletin 1926 says 55 ft, NRHP 68 ft, USLHS 67 ft base to lantern centre; candlepower 800,000 (Bulletin) vs 1.1 million (NRHP); area 12 vs 17.79 acres; stated in text. Lens origin disputed (NRHP: via Alaska 1914; LighthouseFriends doubts). NRHP text mentions a 1 May 1980 ceremony though dated 1977; the form seems to have been updated. USLHS lists Joseph May as first assistant 1942-45, LighthouseFriends as second assistant. Keeper dispute, pennant, automation 1971, ghost timeline and May's reluctance come only from LighthouseFriends (which cites district files and newspapers); not independently verified. Wikipedia consulted only as a lead. Roster is from the USLHS archive lines; 'Point Vicente' vs 'Vincente' spelling changed 1933 per LighthouseFriends. 1918 Bulletin item date: volume 1918, issue month not confirmed. Bulletin 1926 is two-column OCR; quotes taken from single lines. Coast Guard-era names (post-1948) kept to the roster only.
